column1: # forge model registry — single source of truth for alias resolution.
#   alias    short name you type in --dwarf / --qa
#   harness  which CLI runs it: codex | claude | openclaude | opencode | antigravity | grok
#   model    the exact model id that harness expects
#   effort   which reasoning efforts this pairing accepts, in one of four forms:
#              <=X      any effort on the harness ladder up to and including X
#              a,b,c    exactly these efforts and no others (gaps are real: some
#                       models offer low and high but not medium)
#              none     this model takes no effort flag at all; passing one errors
#              -        harness has no validated ladder; forwarded verbatim
#   timeout  OPTIONAL fifth column: the watchdog limit in seconds for this pairing.
#            Leave it off (existing rows do) or write `-` for "no opinion", which falls
#            through to the built-in 2700. `0` disables the watchdog for this pairing.
#            Precedence, highest first: --timeout, the FORGE_TIMEOUT environment
#            variable (both used as given, and `0` there still disables), then this
#            column, then 2700. Only this column and the built-in value are scaled by the
#            effort that finally runs (after clamping): up to high x1, xhigh x4/3,
#            max/ultra/ultracode x2. The result and its source are recorded as
#            Commented examples (not enabled; write the real number for your model):
# FORGE_REGISTRY=<file> points dispatch at a different registry (useful for trying a
# row without editing this one); the capability cache keys on the file actually used.
# An effort outside the accepted set is clamped to the nearest lower one that is
# accepted (and reported), rather than failing a dispatch the user already paid
# to start. A word that is not a recognized effort at all is still an error.
# Row order is meaningful: the FIRST row for an alias is that alias's default
# harness. `--dwarf sol` means sol on codex; `--dwarf sol:high:openclaude` moves
# the same model to a different harness.
# An alias is ONE model on every harness: every row of an alias names the same model
# family and version (a provider prefix such as github-copilot/ or a -preview suffix
# aside). A harness that only serves another version gets a versioned alias
# (`opus-4.6`, `grok-4.6`), never a row under the newer name; tests/test_model_registry.py
# fails on an alias whose rows disagree.
# An alias with no row here is not an error — it is passed through as a literal
# model id, but only when you name the harness explicitly (forge cannot guess a
# default harness for a model it has never heard of).
# The terra before 6.1. Dispatches recorded as `terra` on this model are counted under
# terra-5.6, not under the newer terra (forge_dataset/names.py).
# The sol and astra before 6.2 (#180), kept the same way.
# Claude models by exact id, not the claude CLI's moving `opus`/`sonnet` names, so the
# approval table, statistics and forge-ui show the version that runs. A new Claude release is
# a registry edit: move the alias and keep the old model under `<alias>-<version>`.
# Older Claude models some harnesses still serve. An alias names one model on every harness
# (tests/test_model_registry.py checks it), so these have aliases of their own.
# Antigravity (agy). Gemini models take effort as a flag on the UNSUFFIXED id;
# the suffixed ids agy lists (gemini-3.7-flash-low) conflict with --effort.
